speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the number of HDB flat owners who gave up their new BTO flats in 2018, broken down by flat type; (b) what are the reasons for owners giving up their new BTO flats; and (c) whether their deposits are forfeited.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These measures are in place to ensure that buyers are serious when they apply for a flat, and do not deprive others who are in urgent need of buying a flat.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: And based on percentage, are there more second-timers that gave up BTO flats than the first-timers?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Thirdly, are there plans to pick up the profile of Singaporeans who give up their BTO flats so that we can have a simple profile at the point of application and counsel them accordingly so as to minimise the chances of them giving up their BTO flats?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But these are not that many because, very often, when they have these difficulties, our first recourse is to give them more time to sell the flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And, very often, with more time, they are able to sell the flat and then move on to their next flat that they have purchased.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we continue to analyse each of these cases and, as I said earlier, we are flexible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If there are genuine reasons, if there are financial difficulties, we will have different ways of helping them.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Does HDB suffer losses when the flats are resold?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The third question is: instead of forfeiting 5% of the purchase flat price, would HDB consider charging an appropriate administration fee, considering that HDB is not a commercial entity and, really, if there are no losses suffered by HDB, would there be a lighter penalty imposed?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Otherwise, the flat buyers do suffer quite a heavy loss for losing 5% of the flat price and considering that he also has a one-year time bar imposed on him.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, they are all eventually sold through the SBF exercise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As for why 5% and whether there are other mechanisms, at the end of the day, as I have said, we need a mechanism that ensures buyers consider very carefully the flat purchase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a major commitment; a major commitment for the flat buyer as a couple or as a single, and it is a major financial commitment as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we want to have that in place to ensure that buyers take it very seriously and are also mindful that, when they make a flat purchase, it is a commitment on their part.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If they were to apply and unwind it later, they are, in fact, depriving others who may want the flat more urgently.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is not so much a loss on the Government but, in fact, they are depriving others of an opportunity to get a flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But, as I have said, we do exercise flexibility and if there are individual cases that for some reason or another decide not to proceed with the application, they can put up the case and we will look at it on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Minister, I am speaking for the non-first-time home owners.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How does the Ministry of National Development propose to help residents who, as home owners, have genuine difficulty in selling their homes because of the Ethnic Integration policy?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Minister, what I want to raise is for joint applicants.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What if something happens, say, if someone passes on or for whatever other reason, would HDB allow them to continue to purchase the flat, that is to say, as a result, they do not fulfil the conditions?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And if they cannot, would a special waiver be given not to impose a penalty on them for such unfortunate cases?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And if in the event the eligibility conditions are not met and the applicant chooses not to proceed, we will certainly be prepared to consider waiver of the forfeiture.
